The interface was updating and one browser could not tell. Two server-side causes, both fixed.

## 🐛 Fixed

- **A new build could keep showing the old interface.** An embedded file has no modification time, so the server sent no `Last-Modified`, and it was not sending an `ETag` either. That leaves a browser with no validator at all: it may keep the bundle it already has for as long as it likes, and a reload is entitled to answer out of its own cache without asking. Nothing looks wrong from outside, because nothing is wrong outside; the stale copy is in one browser. Every embedded file now carries a SHA-256 of its own bytes as its `ETag`.
- **A bundle that no longer exists was answered with the page, not a 404.** The single-page fallback exists so that reloading a sub-page reaches the interface's own router. Applied under `assets/` it turned "this file is gone" into "here is some HTML, with a 200", so a browser holding an old page asked for its old bundle and was handed a web page where it expected a script. It fails silently and goes on showing what it had. The same trap was already closed for `/api/` and was still open one directory over.

## ⚡ Improved

- **Two cache rules that pull apart on purpose.** The page itself gets `no-cache`, which means "ask before using" rather than "do not store": one conditional request per load, almost always answered `304` with no body. Everything under `assets/` is content-hashed by the build, so it gets a year and `immutable` and is never asked about again, because a changed file arrives under a different name.

## Note

If the interface still looks unchanged after updating to this build, empty the browser cache once (Ctrl+Shift+R, or Ctrl+F5). A copy already stored without any validator cannot be reached by a fix that arrives after it. From this build on it cannot happen again.
